newsitem.title: THAILAND: Anthrax-hit Thailand monitors Australian outbreak.
newsitem.headline: Anthrax-hit Thailand monitors Australian outbreak.

text.p: Anthrax-hit Thailand will closely monitor a similar outbreak of the disease in Australia before taking any steps against beef and dairy imports from that country, a Health Ministry official said on Thursday.

"We are still assessing the magnitude of the epidemic," the official told Reuters. "Although we heard that the anthrax outbreak is limited to certain areas and is now under control, we will still monitor the situation closely and will take necesssary measures if need be."

More than 80 percent of the beef that Thailand imports comes from Australia and the United States, and Australian meat accounts for more than 40 percent of the total. Most of the imported beef is used by hotels and restaurants.
Anthrax is an infectious disease that affects animals, particularly cattle and sheep, and can infect humans. It causes skin infection, diarrhoea and fever, and can be fatal if it infects the brain.

The outbreak of cattle anthrax earlier this week in the southern Australian state of Victoria appeared to be under control after a massive vaccination programme, a spokesman for the state's Department of Natural Resources and Environment said on Thursday.

In Thailand, four cows died after anthrax broke out last week among cattle in Bangkok and in Sukhothai province, about 450 km (270 miles) north of the capital. At least 19 people were infected after consuming diseased meat, livestock and health ministry officials said.
But Thai officials insisted that the anthrax outbreak was under control and was localised.

"Medical teams have been dispatched into the areas to vaccinate the animals and cure the patients. This is a curable disease, and everything is under complete control," said the Health Ministry official.
"In both places, the anthrax cases were found in illegal slaughter houses, where people killed the animals and distributed the meat among their community and not for the market," the official said.
Thai beef is mostly consumed locally and only a small amount is exported to Malaysia.

"We export the cattle to Malaysia from the south and the Livestock Department has declared the southern part of the country as a disease-free zone for cattle nearly 10 years," a department official said.
